import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Set up the matplotlib figure and subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))
fig.suptitle('Iris Flower Measurements by Species', fontsize=16)

# Plot 1: Sepal Length vs. Sepal Width
sns.scatterplot(
    ax=axes[0],
    data=df,
    x='sepal_length',
    y='sepal_width',
    hue='species',
    s=80, # Marker size
    alpha=0.8,
    palette='viridis' # Color palette
)
axes[0].set_title('Sepal Dimensions', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Sepal Length (cm)', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Sepal Width (cm)', fontsize=12)
axes[0].grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
axes[0].legend(title='Species')

# Plot 2: Petal Length vs. Petal Width
sns.scatterplot(
    ax=axes[1],
    data=df,
    x='petal_length',
    y='petal_width',
    hue='species',
    s=80, # Marker size
    alpha=0.8,
    palette='viridis' # Color palette
)
axes[1].set_title('Petal Dimensions', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Petal Length (cm)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Petal Width (cm)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
axes[1].legend(title='Species')

# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping titles/labels
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95]) # Adjust rect to make space for suptitle

# Save the figure
